title: Out-of-Network Prior Authorization Approval Conditions
content:
**Network access policy.** An out-of-network service under Prairie Ridge Health Plan Prior Authorization is approved only when no in-network provider can deliver it within the class's distance standard in miles or within the class's appointment wait standard in days, and, where the class requires a single case agreement, only after the provider signs a single case agreement before the start date. An authorized out-of-network service costs the member nothing beyond the in-network copay, the class's member cost share for such a service being its figure beyond that copay. Emergency services never need authorization, in or out of network.

The class settings this rule reads are the class's network access standards: whether approval requires that no in-network provider is available, the distance and wait standards, whether a single case agreement is required, and the member cost share.

## Conditions for approving an out-of-network service

| Condition | Met when |
|---|---|
| No in-network provider available | no in-network provider can deliver the service within the distance standard or within the wait standard |
| Single case agreement, where the class requires one | the out-of-network provider signs it before the start date |

Both rows must hold for the service to be approved; the rule states these as the only route to approval.

## Hypothetical cases

1. In a class with a 60-mile and 30-day standard and a single case agreement requirement, the nearest in-network provider is 80 miles away and the out-of-network provider signed the single case agreement a week before the start date: the conditions hold and the service may be approved.
2. Same class, same distance, but the single case agreement is signed only after the start date: the agreement was not signed before the start date, so the service is not approved on this basis.
3. A member receives emergency services from an out-of-network hospital: emergency services never need authorization.

## Member cost

For an authorized out-of-network service the member pays nothing beyond the in-network copay.
